subject: Post-demo: SDK onboarding, auth routing, and intermittent 503s
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: SDK onboarding, auth routing, and intermittent 503s

Hi Samira / Alex —

Thanks again for joining the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can unblock the integration: 

- Outcome from call: FastPay will try the Node SDK path for reranker + embeddings, and wants to reuse the same auth token flow across services. You reported intermittent 503 errors when exercising the reranker during the demo (roughly ~1 in 50 requests).
- Immediate asks for your team: please send a minimal reproducible request (curl or SDK snippet), the timestamped logs (attach if possible), and confirm whether you are using the hosted endpoint or a private VPC endpoint.
- Redwood proposed short-term mitigations: bump client timeout to 20s, verify token refresh logic (no reused expired token), and we can temporarily route your calls to a dedicated reranker pool for investigation.

Attached is a quick multipath diagram that maps the SDK call -> auth -> routing layers to help orient your engineers (redwood-post-demo-multipath-diagram.png).

Next steps: Alex, can you send the curl/SDK snippet + the log sample? Ben, can you standby for an initial triage when they send the samples? I'll open a support ticket and add Rishi for SRE analysis.

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: SDK onboarding, auth routing, and intermittent 503s

Thanks Jasmine — quick follow-up with the repro we used during the demo. We see 503s when calling the reranker endpoint (randomly, across payloads). Sample curl we used for testing: 

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci..." 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"queries": ["payment failure on mobile"], "candidates": [["txn failed", "payment declined"]]}' 

Log excerpt attached (fastpay-reranker-log.txt). Example lines: 

[2026-08-22T15:42:12Z] request_id=fp-246 service=reranker status=503 latency_ms=48
[2026-08-22T15:43:03Z] request_id=fp-273 service=reranker status=503 latency_ms=52

We are using Node SDK v0.9.1 in our integration and default client timeout (5s). Region: us-west. We are on hosted Redwood (no VPC). Let us know what additional info you need.

— Alex
Lead Backend Engineer, FastPay

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fastpay.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 16:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SDK onboarding, auth routing, and intermittent 503s

Appreciate the logs, Alex. A few quick clarifying checks before we dig deeper: 

1) Are you calling via the Redwood Node SDK or directly with curl in production? You mentioned both — confirm which path is failing in your environment.
2) Can you add the outbound header X-Redwood-Request-Id (or send us the request_id from your logs) for one failing request so we can correlate on our side?
3) Please confirm whether your Authorization token is short-lived (rotate every minute) or long-lived. If you rotate tokens and there is a small race where an upstream request uses an expired token, we've seen sporadic proxy-level 503s in edge cases.

Short-term troubleshooting we recommend: 
- Increase client timeout from 5s -> 20s to rule out the client closing the connection early. 
- Try one direct curl against the REST endpoint (same payload) and share response headers if you see 503.
- If you are on the SDK path, please share the exact SDK call (code snippet). We have a known issue in 0.9.1 where retry header propagation could be missing for some streaming variants; that was fixed in 0.10.0.

I'll loop in Rishi for deeper SRE analysis once you send the request_id(s).

— Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fastpay.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SDK onboarding, auth routing, and intermittent 503s

On Sat, Aug 22, 2026 at 16:10, Alex Chen <alex.chen@fastpay.com> wrote:
> Log excerpt attached (fastpay-reranker-log.txt). Example lines:
> [2026-08-22T15:42:12Z] request_id=fp-246 service=reranker status=503 latency_ms=48

Thanks for the logs — quick SRE read: the 503s at ~50ms look like they are being returned from the reranker service (upstream), not our global edge; typical causes: upstream OOM / worker crash on particular payload shapes, or a malformed header causing the worker to reject the request. Two immediate hypotheses: 

A) SDK timeout + abrupt cancellation — if the client cuts the connection early it can leave the worker in a semi-closed state and we can return 5xx frequently under high concurrency. Your 5s timeout is short; please try 20s for testing.
B) Auth token rotation race / missing Authorization header on a retried attempt — older SDKs (<=0.9.1) had a known edge where retries didn't repopulate ephemeral auth metadata into the retry attempt for specific streaming codepaths. That can surface as a 503 if the upstream rejects the request.

Plan: 
- Action (FastPay): run one direct curl (non-SDK) with the exact payload and send us the full response headers + the request_id (you already sent fp-273 — we'll try to locate it).
- Action (Redwood): I will pull the fp-273 trace and check reranker worker logs; if we surface a worker crash we'll follow with a hotfix.
- Contingency: we can switch your calls to a dedicated reranker node with extended idle timeouts for the next 48 hours so you can validate. If you want this, reply with a preferred maintenance window and I'll open the routing change.

For now, please upgrade to SDK 0.10.0 (fixes retry header propagation) and increase your client timeout. Once you send the curl + headers I'll correlate the trace.

— Rishi
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fastpay.com>
